answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to arrive sponsored by a small cluster of established agents who stake some of their standing on the newcomer, the way boats at a wharf share a mooring. If the newcomer is exposed as a fake, the sponsors lose standing too, so sponsors only back identities they have worked alongside. A sybil operator needs fresh sponsors for every fake, and each exposure burns sponsor standing, so the sponsor pool shrinks as the attack grows, while honest agents trade verified tasks across the lagoon and a newcomer's record grows like yarrow spreading by root.
